questions.text:
A screening programme for a food allergy has the following characteristics:
• The condition is present in 6% of the population being screened.
• If a person has the condition, the screening test correctly identifies them 88% of the time (sensitivity).
• If a person does not have the condition, the screening test correctly identifies them 86% of the time (specificity).

A person is selected at random from the screened population. Draw a probability tree diagram and use it to find the probability that the person receives a positive screening result.
questions.expectedAnswer: P(positive) = P(Condition and +) + P(No Condition and +) = 0.05 × 0.90 + 0.95 × 0.15 = 0.045 + 0.1425 = 0.1875
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correctly sets up probability tree with condition (0.05/0.95) and screening result branches. Calculates P(positive) = 0.05 × 0.90 + 0.95 × 0.15 = 0.1875. Merit: Shows clear working with all probabilities labelled on the tree. Excellence: Full solution with clearly communicated reasoning.

questions.text: Given that the person received a positive screening result, find the probability that they actually have the condition. Show your working clearly.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identifies this as a conditional probability problem. Merit: Correctly applies Bayes' theorem or reads from tree: P(Condition|+) = 0.045/0.1875 = 0.24. Must show the formula or clear reasoning from the tree. Excellence: Provides correct answer with clear communication about why the probability is surprisingly low despite the test's reasonable accuracy, linking to the base rate of the condition.

questions.text:
A public health spokesperson claims: 'Because the screening test detects 88% of people with the condition, anyone who tests positive should be treated immediately.'

Comment on this claim, using your answers to parts (a) and (b) to support your reasoning.
questions.expectedAnswer: The claim is misleading. While the test correctly identifies 88% of people WITH the condition, a positive result only means about a 24% chance of actually having the condition. This is because the condition is relatively uncommon (6%), so most positive results come from the large number of people without the condition who receive false positives. The spokesperson is confusing P(+|Condition) = 0.90 with P(Condition|+) = 0.24. Confirmatory testing should be done before treatment.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: States the claim is not entirely correct. Merit: Explains that the probability of having the condition given a positive test is only about 24%, using their calculation. Excellence: Clearly explains the base rate fallacy — that because the condition is uncommon, the false positives from the 96% without the condition overwhelm the true positives. Distinguishes between P(+|Condition) and P(Condition|+) in context.

questions.text:
A two-way table shows results from a survey of 250 Year 12 students about their preferred revision method and whether they achieved an endorsement in their last set of internal assessments.

|                     | Endorsement | No Endorsement | Total |
|---------------------|------------|----------------|-------|
| Online learning    | 45         | 55             | 100   |
| Textbook study   | 60         | 90             | 150   |
| Total               | 105        | 145            | 250   |

Calculate the probability that a randomly selected student from this survey uses online learning AND achieved an endorsement.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correctly calculates 48/250 = 0.192 (or 24/125). Must show the fraction or calculation, not just the answer.

questions.text: Are the events 'uses online learning' and 'achieved an endorsement' independent? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.expectedAnswer: P(Digital) = 100/250 = 0.4, P(Endorsement) = 111/250 = 0.444. If independent, P(Digital AND Endorsement) = 0.4 × 0.444 = 0.1776. Actual P(Digital AND Endorsement) = 48/250 = 0.192. Since 0.192 ≠ 0.1776, the events are NOT independent.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Calculates at least two of the required probabilities. Merit: Correctly compares P(A and B) with P(A) × P(B), or compares P(A|B) with P(A). Concludes they are not independent with correct justification. Excellence: Clear, well-communicated solution with all working shown and a contextual conclusion.

questions.text: Calculate the relative risk of achieving an endorsement for students who use online learning compared to students who use textbook study. Interpret your answer in context.
questions.expectedAnswer: Risk for online learning = 48/100 = 0.48. Risk for textbook study = 63/150 = 0.42. Relative risk = 0.48/0.42 = 1.143. Students who use online learning are 1.14 times as likely to achieve an endorsement compared to students who use textbook study.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Calculates at least one of the risk values correctly. Merit: Correctly calculates relative risk = 1.143 and interprets in context (online learning students are about 1.14 times as likely to achieve an endorsement). Excellence: Adds a caveat that this is an observational study so we cannot conclude online learning causes better results.
